sentences.text: There were disputes with respect to acquisition of property between the parties, who are interested and the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., (BMRCL) on one hand and there were also disputes between the owner of the land on one hand and M/s. Royal Heritage Apartment Owners' Association on the other insofar as the receipt of compensation.
At the intervention of BMRCL, the Authority has come forward and filed an Affidavit to the effect that the extent of land now sought to be acquired would stand reduced to 119.68 Sq. Mtrs.

The averment in the affidavit filed by the General Manager, (Land Acquisition and Estates), Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd., containing reference to such averment at paras-3 NC: 2023:KHC:24866 and 4 of the Affidavit is extracted hereinbelow for the purpose of clarity.

sentences.text: 5 The BMRCL has also submitted the sketch, copy of which is enclosed at Annexure-'R17' demarcating the extent that would be acquired.

6. The terms that have been agreed to by all the parties before this Court are as follows:-
(i) The aspect of determination of title over the acquired land noticing the dispute between the petitioner NC: 2023:KHC:24866 in W.P.No.490/2023 and the petitioner in W.P.No.16862/2021 would be a matter for adjudication before the Reference Court and upon such adjudication, the entitlement for compensation would be determined.
(ii) The case of petitioner-land owner in W.P.No.490/2023 is that insofar as the acquired land is concerned, he would only want cash compensation and if compensation by way of agreement is entered into in terms of Section 29(2) of KIAD Act, the land loser would be entitled to Rs.2,53,98,033.60 along with interest accruing on the amount to be kept in Fixed Deposit in a Nationalized Bank.

However,
it is agreed by consent of rival claimants that, if upon reference, the ownership and title is held in favour of Royal Heritage Apartment Owners' Association, then in such case in the terms of agreement reached along with BMRCL, it is agreed that the BMRCL would offer other alternative land that is shown in the sketch demarcated in blue box lines which would - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:24866 constitute compensation.
The sketch is enclosed alongwith the memo dated 11.07.2023.

(iii) Insofar as the structures on the land proposed to be acquired consisting of compound wall, gate and security cabin and garbage collection tanks are concerned, the question of correctness on the quantum and determination, is a matter being referred to the Reference Court.
Valuation has been done for the structures by BMRCL.

Insofar as the structures are concerned, BMRCL has quantified compensation in a sum of Rs.5,64,147.93 and as there is difference of opinion as regards the valuation of structures, the said aspect for determination of value is to be done by the Reference Court and the claimants and Authority are at liberty to lead their evidence regarding the same.
(iv) It is made clear that the matter for reference refers to all structures.

BMRCL has asserted that it is only the compound wall, gate and security cabin, however, it is - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:24866 submitted on behalf of petitioners that garbage collection tanks are also existing structures, which require valuation.
The said submission is taken note of.

(vi) In the event, the finding before the Reference Court as regards title is recorded in favour of Royal Heritage Apartment Owners' Association, needless to state - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:24866 that the said amount of Rs.2,53,98,033.60, which would be deposited and interest, if any that has accrued on the Fixed Deposit to be kept in a Nationalized Bank during the pendency of reference proceedings would be refunded to KIADB itself, which in turn may transfer the same to BMRCL which is a matter of adjustment inter se.
It is made clear that BMRCL shall reserve the alternative land detailed in the schedule of the memo intact, till disposal of the reference proceedings.
(vii) The General Award dated 21.12.2021 stated to have been passed despite existence of interim order would stand quashed in light of the statement made hereinabove.
(viii) Needless to state that insofar as quantum of compensation of Rs.2,53,98,033.60, as the same would be on the basis of agreement under Section 29(2), there cannot be any further challenge.

However, it is clarified that insofar as the valuation of structures is concerned,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:24866 the right to challenge the correctness of valuation by the Reference Court is kept open as is permissible under law.
(ix) It is also clarified that on the basis of mutual consent by BMRCL, KIADB and other parties, a sum of Rs.5,64,147.93 would be released to Royal Heritage Apartment Owners' Association,
forthwith.

(vii) The General Award dated 21.12.2021 stated to have been passed despite existence of interim order would stand quashed in light of the statement made hereinabove.
(viii) Needless to state that insofar as quantum of compensation of Rs.2,53,98,033.60, as the same would be on the basis of agreement under Section 29(2), there cannot be any further challenge.
However, it is clarified that insofar as the valuation of structures is concerned,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:24866 the right to challenge the correctness of valuation by the Reference Court is kept open as is permissible under law.
(ix) It is also clarified that on the basis of mutual consent by BMRCL, KIADB and other parties, a sum of Rs.5,64,147.93 would be released to Royal Heritage Apartment Owners' Association,
forthwith.
(x) The names found in Column Nos.2 and 3 of the Notification passed under Section 28(4) of KIAD Act dated 31.01.2021 would stand substituted by the names of petitioner in W.P.No.490/2023 and in W.P.No.16862/2021 by issuing a Corrigendum by the concerned Authority.
The order is being passed on the basis of terms proposed and agreed to by learned counsel appearing for all the parties and on the basis of which the Court has disposed off the Writ Petitions confirming the understanding recorded before the Court by all the parties concerned and their duly authorized representatives affirming the amicable settlement of dispute with consent as per terms incorporated in the order passed by this Court.
It is also clarified that the reservation of alternative land is till the question of title attains finality and the Reference Court to decide regarding the question of title within an outer limit of six months.
All parties to co-operate in the early disposal of the matter before the Reference Court.
It is also directed that the builder M/s. Gopalan Enterprises would be impleaded in the proceedings referred to before the Reference Court.
10. C.C.C.No.1087/2022 (civil) filed by the petitioner in W.P.No.16862/2021 before this Court would be withdrawn as is permissible under law.
Subject to the above directions and observations, the Writ Petitions are disposed off.
